query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Oxidation-induced grain boundary embrittlement governs degradation of the Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing gases, leading to catastrophic failure.
generation.material_initial_state: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix
generation.intervention: Exposure to oxidizing gases at elevated temperatures
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 600-1000°C, gas composition: air or oxygen-rich environment
generation.mechanism: Oxidation-induced grain boundary embrittlement leads to reduced ductility and increased susceptibility to cracking
generation.predicted_outcome: Catastrophic failure due to brittle fracture
generation.baseline: No exposure to oxidizing gases or elevated temperatures
generation.uncertainty: Insufficient data on the specific alloy composition and microstructure, as well as the exact exposure conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled exposure of the alloy to oxidizing and reducing gases at elevated temperatures, with characterization of microstructure and mechanical properties
measurements: Grain boundary oxidation, embrittlement, and cracking
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant grain boundary embrittlement or cracking is observed after exposure to oxidizing gases, the hypothesis is falsified
